```{python}
#| code-fold: show
train_words = set(re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text[:n_train].lower()))


def real_word_share(s):
    words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+", s.lower())
    return sum(w in train_words for w in words) / len(words)


drawn = sample(lm, "MENENIUS:\n", 1000)
drawn_share = real_word_share(drawn)
# The prose below says the draw has speaker names on lines of their own.
assert re.search(r"^[A-Z]+:$", drawn[10:], re.MULTILINE)
print(drawn[:300])
print(drawn_share)
```

Counting a word as a run of letters,
ignoring case,
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$drawn_share)` of the words drawn occur in the training text.
The rest are made-up words.
Like the play,
the draw puts names in capitals followed by a colon on lines of their own,
beyond the one in the prompt.
